findings: HB134 identifies a full-length sheet-steel casing 6 5/8 inches wide, supported by angle irons within the track extensions, with a separate removable outer cap. Maximum width remains 168.275 mm; 3 mm normal stock is an inherited reconstruction assumption, not a printed thickness.
HB134 requires removing the epicyclic gear before the main casing and fixing the casing before remounting that gear. No casing removal or installation path is qualified by this static trial.
SNL31 allocates fourteen 1/2 x 1 inch cap bolts across the vehicle; the selected seven sets per cap and nested rivet counts are retained. Global and nested SNL167 rivet schedules remain unreconciled.
SNL170 assigns eleven rivets to each M2003/M1592 wall joint. The handbook bolted mounting/removal description and this explicit rivet allocation remain a source tension.
HB185 places M1584 packing under the cleat foot. Existing M1585/M1586 identity and quantity conflicts and SNL191 global versus nested beading-rivet totals remain open.

The SNL2 overlay retains the original global calibration. The revised small end rises while the roller end stays fixed; the lower tangent becomes nearly horizontal. The source small-gear center remains below the revised modeled station, so this view does not establish the station as historical truth.

No independently dimensioned casing outline establishes the local taper, seam position, hole pattern or exact end profiles. They remain explicit approximations constrained by chain, stock and neighboring material.
decision: Retain the rebuilt casings as the next development baseline for the conditional mean-axis placement; complete transmission attachment and preservation gates before standard integration.
